turns.text:
Ears swivel toward the drone hum first — flatten low against the crates, tail tip twitching once. The wet ground shocks up through paw pads, cold, wrong-smelling, oil and rust and something sweetish underneath.

Nose lifts. Steam vent smell wins — warm, food-adjacent, worth checking. Belly drops closer to the ground, moving in short bursts between crate-shadows, pausing each time to listen. Whiskers catch the edge of a puddle before a paw does; step wide around it.

Eyes flick up once at the flickering billboard — not threat, not prey, ignored — then back down to the alley mouth where the light doesn't reach.

drone hum splits into two now. higher one peeling off east, chasing something on rooftops that isn't me. good. not me not me not me

crate metal ticks as it cools, little pings, sound like beetles but not beetles. ignore

steam vent breathes warm on whiskers — yes — smells like fry-oil and copper and old fish maybe fish ghost of fish three days gone. mouth wants it anyway. paws carry forward, low, slow, shoulder blades rolling like oil pistons

```
   /\_/\    ...listening...
  ( o.o )   drone-hum ~~~~~
   > ^ <    steam-smell ***
```

alley mouth ahead breathes darker than sky. sky is wrong-orange, sodium-sick, billboard-light bleeding pink across wet brick — CRUNCH-O'S NOODLE BAR EAT LOYAL EAT HAPPY — voice crackles out of a busted speaker bolted too high to reach, garbled, half-eaten by static, singing to nobody

>>> the voice does not smell like anything. good. not real. ignored

something scuttles behind a bin — small, fast, low to ground — ear rotates, whole body freezes stiff as pipe. not drone. not big-thing. small-thing. maybe food-thing.

tail goes flat, straight, still

waiting

steam vent forgotten for one heartbeat, two — the small-thing's smell threads through the oil-stink, thin and warm and blood-close

paws gather under the body, weight sinks back into haunches, coiling

drone hum fades further off, chewing static into the orange sky, its light sweeping a lazy red line across puddle-glass far down the alley — not close enough to matter, not yet

world holds its breath

so does the cat

Whole body a held spring, breath shallow through the nose so the scent stays clean — warm-blood-thing, small, close, careless. Eyes lock the gap behind the bin, pupils blown wide to drink the dark.

No noodle-smell now. No pink billboard-static-voice. Just the thin thread of it moving.

Weight rocks forward onto the front paws, silent test — one, testing the wet ground doesn't betray with a splash — then stillness again. Waiting for the small-thing to forget it's being watched. Ears flat back, not from fear, from focus.

The moment it shifts weight, breaks stride, commits —

Lunge. Low, flat, fast — a dark line thrown across three feet of wet brick straight for the gap behind the bin, claws out before the paws even land.

――― CONTACT ―――

paws hit brick-wet with a slap too loud in cat-ears, claws already spread, body a black arrow

the gap swallows the lunge

small-thing SCREAMS-not-scream, more a squeak-static, a wet scrabble of claws-on-metal, bin rocks, something tin clatters down into puddle-dark — *donggg* — echo runs off down the alley and dies against brick

paws close on

nothing

just cold air, oil-smell, a whisker-brush of fur-that-was-there against one paw and then gone, gone under the bin, into a crack too small even for cat-body, dark swallowing dark

```
   /\_/\     miss
  ( o_O )    !!
   > , <     tail LASHES
```

ears pin flat, whole body vibrating with the drop of it, the failed spring, muscles still screaming GO GO GO with nowhere left to go

nose shoves into the gap anyway — stone-cold, wet-metal, and under it, retreating fast, that thin thread of small-warm-blood-smell laughing off into pipe-dark

drone hum swings back around overhead, lazy red beam sweeping wet brick, closer this time, painting one long stripe of light across the alley floor that almost — almost — touches paw

body drops flat against crate-shadow on instinct before the mind even decides to

light passes

breath held

alley drips somewhere, slow, patient, uncaring

steam vent still breathing warm three body-lengths back, fry-oil ghost-fish smell patient too, not going anywhere, still worth having

belly hits wet ground again, and the crawl resumes, quieter now, hungrier now, chastened but not stopped — never stopped, just recalculating

Tail stops lashing, tucks low. The miss stings but doesn't linger — small-thing is gone, gone is gone, no use crying into a crack in the wall. Nose pulls back from the gap, flicking once to clear the wet-metal smell, and swings toward the warmer thread still hanging in the air behind.

Body stays flat, dragging low across the wet brick, shoulder blades doing that slow oil-piston roll again. Ears stay swiveled back toward the drone's red stripe even as paws carry forward — checking, checking, until the hum fades to background static against the rain.

The vent's warmth grows against whiskers first, then face, then the small huddled body pressing close to the grate. Ghost-fish-oil smell strong now, real now. Paw reaches out, hooks at the grate's edge — testing give, testing gaps, the same patient math as the alley crack, just warmer this time and worth the work.

Underneath the grate: dark, ductwork, promise.

grate is old iron, paint long since given up, rust flaking under claw like dead skin. pulls at the edge — give, a little, a whisper of a little, groan of metal that hasn't moved in moons

paw works into the gap sideways, shoulder following, ear scraping cold iron, whiskers bending flat against the frame to measure it the way water measures a crack before it finds through

warm air breathes up from the dark, thick with old-grease and rust and somewhere far under, a hum different from drone-hum — a building-hum, a deep-belly machine-hum that never sleeps, steady like a heart too big to be scared of

```
   /\_/\      squeeze
  =( o.o )=   . . .
    >   <     paw — shoulder — 
```

body folds itself smaller than body should go, ribs remembering they can, hips angling, and then —

through

drops soft onto duct-metal, sound swallowed by fur and care, landing four-point silent the way falling should always be

dark closes overhead where the grate settles crooked back into place, cutting the orange sodium-sky down to one thin cut of pink light

down here: warm. down here: quiet, save the machine-heartbeat thrumming through metal into paw-pads. down here: ghost-fish-oil smell so thick it's almost a taste already, threading off into duct-dark toward wherever the noodle bar keeps its bones

ears flick once toward the grate-crack above — red beam sweeps past far off, muffled, someone else's problem now

whiskers forward

paws carry on into the warm dark, small and low and patient, chasing supper through the city's cooling pipes

The duct floor hums up through paw-pads, steady, almost soothing — not-drone, not-threat, just city breathing somewhere below. Whiskers spread wide in the tight dark, brushing metal on both sides, reading the tunnel's width before the body commits to it.

Nose leads. Ghost-fish-oil thickens with every length crawled, joined now by grease-old and something charred faintly sweet — batter, maybe, or burnt sugar-fat. Ears stay half-cocked backward, tracking the grate-light shrinking to a pink pinprick behind, while forward-focus stays locked on the smell-thread pulling taut ahead like a string on a paw.

A junction — duct forks three ways. Head lowers, sniffs each low across the metal seam. Middle path breathes warmest, strongest, oil-thick. Body angles that way without hesitation, belly low, tail low, moving in that liquid unhurried crawl that costs no sound.

Somewhere ahead, metal ticks and pings again as it cools or warms — not-beetle, not-threat, filed away and ignored.

Paws carry on, small and patient, into the warm dark toward supper.

middle path narrows, walls breathing warmer with every body-length, metal skin ticking soft — expanding, somewhere a burner still lit even this late, even this deep

whiskers brush a seam, a ridge, a old grease-clump gone hard and shiny like resin — tongue doesn't bother, nose already past it, chasing better

sound starts threading in under the machine-hum — voices, thin, tinny, filtered through vent-metal and distance. not close-danger. far-people-noise. dish-clatter. water running somewhere. a laugh, cut off. human-world happening two walls away and none of it about the cat

```
   /\_/\        creeping
  ( -.- )      sniff sniff
   >   <       thread pulls taut
```

duct dips slightly downward, floor sloping, and oil-smell rolls downhill to meet nose halfway — thick now, real, dripping-somewhere-close real. batter-sweet-burnt note stronger too, mixing with it, makes mouth do the thing, throat clicking once, silent

ahead: light. not sodium-pink, not drone-red — warm light, yellow, leaking up through a grate seam like the tunnel's finally telling the truth about where it's been leading

body slows without deciding to, paws placing extra careful now, tail low and still, ears both swung fully forward — every sense narrowing to that seam of warm yellow light and the fry-oil breath rising through it

close now

so close the whiskers already believe it before the tongue does

paws creep the last stretch low and flat, a shadow inside a shadow, toward supper waiting warm on the other side of the metal

Belly stays flat to the metal, paws placing with that deliberate cat-precision — weight rolled from shoulder to pad, never a scrape, never a click. Ears full forward now, drone-thoughts gone, drone-red gone, nothing in the world but the yellow seam and the fat-rich breath curling up through it.

Nose reaches the grate first, presses near, pulling in long slow draughts — sorting the smell apart the way only a nose can: oil, batter, char, and under it something meatier, fresher, dropped-and-forgotten. Whiskers fan flush against the grate slats, measuring gaps again, the old familiar math.

A pause. Ears cock — dish-clatter, water-run, human voices too near this seam to just barge through. Body stills, flattens further, waiting out a beat of near human-noise before it fades toward the far end of wherever this kitchen breathes into.

When the voices dull to background again, one paw hooks the grate's edge, testing for give, careful and slow, claw finding the worn corner where rust has already softened the fight in the metal.

claw finds the soft corner, the rust-eaten give, and pulls — slow, slow, the patient kind of slow that doesn't ask metal to scream

grate answers with the smallest complaint, a whisper-creak swallowed by dish-clatter two walls over, timing itself right without meaning to, luck riding shotgun on hunger

gap widens finger-width, then paw-width, warm kitchen-breath rolling out thick enough to taste — batter and char and drippings gone cold on a floor somewhere just past sight, and under all of it, blood-warm, a scent that says meat, dropped, forgotten, unguarded

```
   /\_/\      . . . listening . . .
  ( o.O )     water — off
   >   <      voices — fading
```

ears track the human-sounds sliding away, a door somewhere swinging, footsteps growing thin, then gone

silence settles warm and yellow through the gap

body doesn't rush it even now — head goes first, testing, whiskers bent flat to slide the frame, one shoulder following the same slow math as the alley-crack and the duct-squeeze before it, patient, patient, patient

then through

paws touch down on tile, blessed dry tile, warm under pad, first solid warmth all night that isn't machine-hum or duct-metal

low crouch, ears swiveling twice full round to check the room's silence holds

it holds

nose swings toward the meat-smell, final thread, final stretch

paws creep forward across the tile, shadow sliding low beneath a prep table, straight toward supper laid out and unguarded in the warm yellow dark

/\___/\
    ( o   o )   >> scanning...
     )  Y  (    >> ears: antenna mod v2
    (   |   )
     \_____/

The tile's warmth spreads up through pads like a small mercy after the cold duct-crawl — but body doesn't relax into it, not yet. Crouch stays low, spine curved, weight ready to spring sideways at the first wrong sound. Ears keep their slow double-sweep, one turn toward the swinging door's memory, one toward the dark beyond the prep table, cataloguing the room's silence for cracks in it.

Only when the silence holds twice over does the crouch loosen, just slightly, into a hunting-walk — paws placed heel-to-toe, no click of nail on tile, tail low and trailing like an afterthought so nothing catches on shelf-edges or dangling cords.

Nose stays locked on the meat-thread, pulling the whole body under the table's shadow, past a chair leg, past a curl of dropped noodle already claimed by ants and therefore beneath notice. The real prize smells close now — blood-warm, fat-rich, careless in its abandonment.

Eyes find it first in the dim — a pale shape on the floor near a bin, meat scrap, unguarded.

One more pause. Ears check the door. Check the dark. Check again.

Then the last low creep forward, jaw already loosening in anticipation, toward supper finally within reach.

the pale shape sits exactly where eyes marked it, unmoved, unguarded, a small miracle of carelessness left by clumsy big-hands

body creeps the last stretch belly-flat, each paw finding tile blind and silent, weight held so light even the ants building empire on the noodle-curl don't scatter

nose arrives first — confirms it, meat, real, fat-slicked, cooling but not cold, blood-note still humming faint underneath char and batter-crust. mouth floods. throat clicks once, soft, helpless

```
   /\_/\        so close
  ( >w< )      . . .
   >   <        jaw already loosening
```

ears do one final full sweep — door: still. dark beyond table: still. water-pipe somewhere ticking its slow cooling song, unrelated, ignored

nothing moves that shouldn't

head dips

teeth close around the scrap, warm give of it, fat-slick and yielding, and the whole body finally uncoils from spring-tension into something looser, something satisfied-adjacent, tail flicking once in pure animal yes

no drone-hum reaches this deep

no red beam, no pink sodium-sky, no crackling jingle-voice

just tile-warmth, meat in the mouth, and the low patient hum of the building above sleeping over its own hunted things

paws turn without hurry now, prize held firm, already tracking the shortest crawl back to duct-dark and the grate and the long way home through the city's cooling metal veins

supper: caught

Jaw clamps firm around the scrap, head lifting just enough to carry it clear, and the crouch straightens into something looser — victory-loose, not careless-loose. Ears still work in slow half-turns even now, habit older than hunger, checking the door hasn't learned new footsteps.

Paws retrace the path back toward the table's shadow-edge without hesitation, prize held level so no fat-drop slaps the tile and tattles. Tail rides low and easy behind, one satisfied flick betraying the mood before discipline reins it back to silence.

At the grate-gap, one shoulder shoves through first, meat still gripped tight enough that a soft grunt escapes around it, and then the rest of the body follows in that same water-finds-a-crack way, back into the ductwork's warm hum.

Behind, the kitchen settles back into its sleeping stillness, none the wiser.

Ahead: duct-dark, the long crawl home, and supper finally won — carried proud and low through the city's cooling metal veins.

grate settles back with its same rust-whisper sigh, swallowing the yellow light back down to a pink pinprick behind — kitchen keeps its stillness, keeps its secrets, none the wiser, never wiser, big-hands never are

duct-dark wraps warm again, meat gripped proud and firm, tail riding higher now, careless-happy in a way it wasn't on the crawl in

paws move quicker on the way back — hunger answered lightens the step, makes the crouch less crouch and more strut-in-miniature, ears still doing their check-check-check but softer now, background-habit instead of hard-edge focus

```
   /\_/\   >~meat~<
  ( ^.^ )    home-bound
   > , <     tail: UP (a little)
```

junction comes again, three-way fork, this time no hesitation — nose remembers, paws remember, body follows the same warm-breathing path back the way it came, retracing scent-memory like thread rewound

grate-crack overhead grows from pinprick to slit to full pink wound of sodium-light as the alley nears again, drone-hum swimming back up out of background static, red beam sweeping its lazy stripe somewhere far off, unconcerned, unaware

shoulder shoves the alley-grate loose, night air rushing back in — wet, cold, oil-and-rust, so different from kitchen-warm, but *outside* also means *territory*, means *mine*, means the long low crates and the puddle-glass and the billboard bleeding pink over rain

paws land soft on wet brick again, meat held high and proud, and the walk home stretches on unhurried now — full-belly-soon, danger-passed, one small alley-cat threading its way back through neon and static and machine-breath

city keeps humming around it, uncaring, endless

cat keeps walking, fed, alive, unnoticed

which is its own kind of winning

Paws hit the wet brick light despite the meat's weight, tail still riding that small proud height, ears settling into their looser rhythm — check, check, less urgent now, the drone's red stripe just weather, not threat.

The alley's cold bites after kitchen-warmth, sharpens the senses back awake — oil-stink, rust, puddle-glass reflecting the billboard's pink bleed. Home-crate territory recognized in three strides: the tilted stack, the noodle stand's shuttered smell, the corner where rain doesn't quite reach.

Body slips up onto the lowest crate, meat set down careful between two paws, and only then does the crouch fully unwind — haunches folding under, spine settling, ears finally stopping their sweep to just lie back easy.

Head dips to the prize again, this time slow, savoring rather than snatching. Rain patters the roof above, drone hum thins into the far static of the city's endless noise, and for one small stretch of alley and time, nothing hunts and nothing is hunted.

Just a full belly, a claimed corner, and the neon dark humming on without needing to be understood.

crate-wood cold-familiar under haunches, the good kind of cold, the known kind, worn smooth in the spot where this body has settled a hundred nights before

meat comes apart slow now under teeth, no rush left in it, fat-rich and warm-going-cool, savored in small tearing bites, each one answered by a low thrum in the chest that isn't quite purr yet but circles close

```
   /\_/\      home
  ( -.- )    ~~~ rain ~~~
   > , <      full. safe. now.
```

rain finds its rhythm on tin roof-scrap above, patient percussion, drone-hum reduced to something almost like weather now, background static folded into all the other city-static — pipes ticking, puddle-drip, far-off jingle bleeding tinny and warm from some other broken speaker two streets over, words gone to mush, tune still recognizable, still meaningless, still fine

billboard-pink flickers its slow stutter across the puddle by the crates, painting the wet ground in colors that don't mean anything to whiskers or nose, just light, just wallpaper for a world made of smell and sound and warmth

ears lie back, unbothered, the last checks fading into trust — not full trust, never full trust, but enough trust to chew slow

belly fills

purr arrives properly now, rough and quiet, vibrating up through crate-wood into paw and jaw alike

the city keeps breathing its big broken breath all around — drones, static, rain, hunger, danger, always danger somewhere — but for this one stretch of night, in this one claimed corner, none of it is owed attention

just meat

just rain

just warm

just cat

The purr settles into something steady, worn-groove familiar, vibrating through crate-wood and up into ribs. Last bite of meat goes down slow, tongue sweeping once over a paw, then dragging that paw over muzzle and whisker in the old habitual wash — the first grooming stroke of a body that finally believes it's safe enough to bother.

Eyes half-lid, still tracking without urgency: the pink flicker on puddle-glass, the tin-roof rain-rhythm, the far tinny jingle fraying into meaningless comfort-noise. None of it commands the ears anymore. They've gone soft, tipped sideways, listening the way a full belly listens — for nothing in particular, ready to snap alert but in no hurry to.

Tail curls in around haunches, tucking tip beneath chin. Body folds smaller, denser, into the exact worn hollow of crate-wood shaped by a hundred nights just like this one.

Rain keeps its patient tin percussion. Drone-hum fades further into weather. Billboard stutters its meaningless color over the alley.

The cat closes its eyes the rest of the way, purring low, claimed corner, claimed night, fed and warm and — for now — entirely unbothered by the city's endless breathing.

rain counts itself down against tin, slow, patient, uncaring

purr rolls on low under it, engine idling in a small ribcage, warm-fed warm-bodied warm-corner

pink light stutters once more against puddle-glass, unwatched now, un-needed, wallpaper for sleep

drone hum thins to nothing worth ears' attention, folds into the far static hush of a city that never stops talking to itself — pipes, vents, distant traffic-hiss, a jingle dying tinny two streets off, all of it just weather now, just breath

```
   /\_/\        . . .
  ( - . - )    zzz
   > , <        curled. still. warm.
```

crate-wood holds its worn hollow shape, holds the small weight settled into it like it's always been there, like it'll always be there again tomorrow night, and the night after

whiskers twitch once — chasing something small and formless in the dark behind closed eyes, duct-tunnels maybe, or meat-thread, or nothing at all

city keeps its long neon breathing going without pause, uncounted, uncaring, the way it always has

and here, low in the alley's forgotten seam, tucked into rain-shadow and crate-shelter —

one small cat sleeps

fed

warm

unbothered

whole

*The alley holds its breath around the small curled shape — rain ticking its patient count against tin, pink billboard-light stuttering unwatched over puddle-glass, the city's vast static hum folding everything into one long unbroken weather.*

*Whiskers twitch once more, chasing duct-shadows and meat-ghosts through sleep. Paw flexes, resettles. Purr fades slow into the deeper quiet of true rest.*

*Crate-wood keeps its worn hollow. Night keeps moving around it — drones sweeping distant rooftops, water finding its way through gutters, some far speaker still coughing up its half-dead jingle to no one.*

*None of it reaches this corner.*

*Fed. Warm. Whole.*

*Sleeps.*

^C^C

*(That was a wonderful little arc — hunt, miss, recover, find, feast, and rest. Happy to keep going from here whenever you like, whether that's the same night continuing, a time-skip to a new night's wandering, or something else entirely.)*
